extracted.intended_audience: covered entities and their compliance officers (health care providers, health systems, health insurers) and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for covered entities to develop, maintain, and implement Section 1557 Policies and Procedures, including nondiscrimination policies, grievance procedures, recordkeeping, and language access procedures, scaled to entity size and complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies and Procedures design and scalability
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and Procedures must be reasonably designed, take into account a covered entity's size, complexity, and the type of health programs or activities provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates are starting points; covered entities should view templates as a beginning and ensure policies reflect appropriate scope. OCR expects the scope and detail to vary according to size, capabilities, costs, operational impact, and composition of patient populations served. The templates may be insufficient for large covered entities given the range in complexity and structure of those entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinator contact information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: §92.8(b), (d), (e), and (f) require the Coordinator's current contact information rather than the Coordinator's name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provisions require sufficient information for an individual to reach the Coordinator; a covered entity may list the position title with a phone number, email address, and mailing address (rather than a specific person's name) to avoid constant edits due to turnover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to review and revise policies
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must review and revise its policies and procedures, as necessary, to ensure they are current and in compliance with section 1557 and this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new paragraph (h) was added explaining covered entities may change policies and procedures at any time, provided the changed policies comply with section 1557 and this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination Policy content and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: A Nondiscrimination Policy must prohibit discrimination, and the description of sex discrimination in the policy should be consistent with the description in §92.101(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR revised §92.8(b) to adjust the explanatory parenthetical for sex to state 'consistent with the scope of sex discrimination described at §92.101(a)(2)' (which includes 'gender identity'). The policy need not explicitly include all forms of sex discrimination to address First Amendment concerns. As a best practice, recipients' Nondiscrimination Policy should reflect any exemptions granted under §92.302.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged additional policies (telehealth, service animals, emergencies, bilingual competency, accessible equipment)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR encourages covered entities to develop policies and procedures related to service animals, protecting civil rights during public health emergencies, assessing bilingual/multilingual staff competency, nondiscriminatory provision of telehealth, and accessible medical diagnostic equipment, but does not require them at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR recognizes benefits but declines to mandate these additional policies due to initial burden; covered entities may adopt such policies to ensure compliance. See discussions of §92.204 (accessible buildings), §92.207 (medical diagnostic equipment), and §92.211 (telehealth nondiscrimination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures requirement (threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities with 15 or more employees are required to have grievance procedures under §92.8(c); entities with fewer than 15 employees are not required but are encouraged to voluntarily implement grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach aligns with OCR's section 504 regulation (45 CFR 84.7(a)). Individuals may still file complaints with OCR even if the covered entity lacks a formal grievance procedure. OCR provides sample grievance procedures on its website, including versions appropriate for smaller entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process accessibility and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity's grievance process must be accessible to individuals with limited English proficiency (LEP) and individuals with disabilities, and information about the availability of grievance procedures and how to file must be included in the Notice of Nondiscrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered entities must include information in the Notice of Nondiscrimination per §92.10(a)(1)(vi) and (vii). The process should be simple, not burdensome, and accessible; OCR recommends filing with OCR if a grievance process is ineffective or overly burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance resolution standard ('prompt and equitable')
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievances must be resolved in a 'prompt and equitable' manner, but OCR declines to impose a single timeframe or to define 'prompt and equitable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR cites consistency with 45 CFR 84.7(b) and 86.8(b). Imposing a single timeframe would not account for differing sizes, resources, and grievance natures. Factors affecting time include the nature of the grievance. OCR may investigate if a grievance is not resolved promptly and equitably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance records retention minimum and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities required to have grievance procedures must retain grievance records for a minimum of three calendar years; retention period starts on the date the covered entity resolves the grievance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §92.8(c)(2) specifies that retained records are those filed pursuant to grievance procedures alleging discrimination based on race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability in health programs or activities. Records must include the name and contact information of the complainant, the alleged discriminatory action and basis(es), the date the grievance was filed, the date the grievance was resolved, and the grievance resolution. OCR decided three years balances burden and investigatory needs; entities may retain longer and may deidentify after the retention period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of grievance submitter identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must keep confidential the identity of the individual who submits a grievance, subject to limited exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR recognizes patient privacy concerns and declined to require deidentification during the retention period. HIPAA-covered entities must also comply with HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules; other covered entities must comply with applicable Federal and State privacy laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of records to retain (actionable / covered grievances only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities need only retain records for grievances received pursuant to their grievance procedures that allege discrimination on protected bases in the covered entity's health programs or activities; employment-related or unrelated grievances need not be retained under §92.8(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the covered entity cannot determine whether a complaint relates to section 1557, it should contact the complainant to obtain sufficient information to investigate or redirect the complaint. A covered entity's dismissal of a grievance constitutes its resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language access procedures requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Language access procedures (§92.8(d)) must assist covered entities in meeting obligations under §92.201, include companions of patients when necessary, and ensure companions are covered by language assistance services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 92.8(d) allows flexibility in how covered entities identify individuals with LEP and procure interpreters/translators (e.g., contract or in-house). Procedures should include contact information for the Coordinator and how employees obtain services of qualified interpreters, translators, and multilingual/bilingual staff. Procedures should ensure access to electronic translated materials (location on network/intranet/website). OCR revised the requirement to no longer require physical locations of translated materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language access operational best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities should analyze service-area language needs, consider documenting a patient's LEP needs in records, and are encouraged (but not required) to develop language access plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developing effective procedures requires some analysis to identify language needs (e.g., top non-English languages and suitable providers). HHS LEP Guidance and other resources (lep.gov, HHS Language Access Plan 2023) are instructive. If an entity's language access plan meets §92.8(d) requirements, a separate procedures document is not required. OCR declines to mandate formal language access plans due to small-entity burdens but encourages them as a best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain current list of qualified bilingual/multilingual staff and electronic materials access
rubrics_metrics.description: Language access procedures must include a current list of qualified bilingual/multilingual staff members and how to access electronic translated materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declined to remove the requirement for a current directory of qualified bilingual staff despite turnover concerns, noting these staff play a critical role. OCR removed the requirement to list physical locations of translated materials and instead requires information on accessing electronic translated materials (network, intranet, or external-facing website).
